question.text: What is the validity period of the NISM Series V-A: Mutual Fund Distributors Certification, after which renewal is required?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the NISM certification framework, the NISM Series V-A: Mutual Fund Distributors Certification has a validity period of 3 years from the date of passing the examination. Before it lapses, the distributor must either re-take the certification exam or complete the prescribed Continuing Professional Education (CPE) requirements to obtain a refreshed certificate. AMFI ARN/EUIN registration depends on holding a valid NISM certification, and so must be renewed in step with it. The Trap: 1 year and 2 years are too short — those validity periods apply to other regulatory registrations, not NISM certifications. 5 years is too long; no NISM certification carries a 5-year validity window. The exam-specific number is 3. Note: The cited NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook pages reviewed in the audit support the prerequisite of valid NISM certification and the timely-renewal requirement for AMFI registration, but do not explicitly state the 3-year validity figure on the pages checked. The 3-year period stated above is drawn from the general NISM certification framework and is consistent with the workbook's renewal language.
